description: `loadAndSet()` runs a `?{}` query and then assigns `@count = rows.length`. A function that performs a reactive assignment is CPS-split (§6.6.9): the query AND the statement that consumes its result run in the server half, and the server half hands back only the cell's final value (§19.9.9.7) — the count, never the rows. E-RI-002 does not fire. (S462: the case id keeps its historical `-pos` suffix; it pinned E-RI-002 until S462.)
rationale: §6.6.9 — "A function that also performs a reactive assignment (`@cell = …`) is CPS-split (§19.9.9) — a CLIENT function with an embedded server round-trip." §19.9.9.7 — within one server batch a cell read sees the batch's own earlier write, and the client applies the write when the batch returns. Until S462 impl#1 refused this shape with E-RI-002 for an IMPLEMENTATION reason, not a SPEC one: its CPS tier classifier did not see the `?{}` attached to the `const` declaration, found no server statement, and so found no split (recorded at S451, docs/changes/s451-boot-u1a/progress.md: "is impl#1's CPS-eligibility answer; under §19.9.5 the same shape is a split"). Provenance: S462 P0 (docs/changes/s462-p0-cps-server-logic-to-client/) — direction of change: newly-accepting; supersedes this case's pre-S462 expectation `codes: ["E-RI-002"]`.
